line.text: The market opened around Dallas −3.5 and has traded in a 3.5-to-4.5 band all week, with most books at −4 or −4.5 by Saturday and the total settling on 50.5 — the highest number on the Week 2 board. The movement toward Dallas has been modest, half a point to a point, which is notable given Dallas lost outright in Week 1. Yahoo's reporting is that sharps took Cowboys −3.5, a better number than is now available, which would explain a drift that then stalled.
line.kalshi: Kalshi has Dallas at 66¢ ask, normalizing to 65.35%, against a best-of-market devigged 65.12% and a lowest-hold single book (Hard Rock, 3.70%) at 64.29%. That is within a quarter of a point of fair. Kalshi and the books are saying the same thing about this game.
line.src: VegasInsider Sep 19; Yahoo Sep 15 and Sep 18

splits.text: Spread: Dallas 65% of tickets but 84% of the MONEY. Total: the Over took 81% of bets and 76% of the money.
A flatly different picture from the same date: Dallas 57% of bets and 57% of handle on the spread — no divergence at all — with 79% of handle on the Over.

And a third: BetMGM's trading desk told Yahoo it was seeing MORE WASHINGTON money than Dallas money on the spread, which it called surprising given the home field, plus 'a little more under money'. Sharps, per the same piece, bet Cowboys −3.5.

line.conflict: Three mutually incompatible reports on the spread: heavy Dallas money, a dead-even market, and more Washington money. They cannot all be true. The only claim every usable source shares is that the OVER is the heavily public side of the total, at 76-81% of money — and even that conflicts with BetMGM reporting more under money. A fourth source, FantasySP, shows an identical 85/15 split across spread, moneyline and total including 85% of money on a +180 underdog; that is implausible and was discarded as a broken feed. The most credible single data point is the Yahoo-sourced statement that sharps bet Cowboys −3.5 — which implies the current −4/−4.5 is past the number professionals wanted.

week1.head: Washington 0-1: lost 24-22 at Philadelphia (Sep 13)
week1.text: Washington covered and lost by two, failing on a late two-point conversion that would have forced overtime. Jayden Daniels went 18 of 24 for 164 with two touchdowns. The problems were structural: Washington allowed an NFL-HIGH 50% PRESSURE RATE, and of its 295 total yards nearly half came on the final two drives — a slow-start team. The defence allowed only 10 first downs but gave up four plays of 30-plus yards. Terry McLaurin, 31, had two catches for 14 yards on four targets under new coordinator David Blough, who had said he wanted him at around ten targets a week. Dan Quinn, Dallas's defensive coordinator from 2021 to 2023, is the head coach.

week1.head: Dallas 0-1: lost 28-20 at the NY Giants on Sunday Night Football (Sep 13)
week1.text: Dak Prescott went 22 of 34 for 175 with a touchdown and a pick, and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were held to 72 combined receiving yards. The defensive numbers are the story: Dallas finished Week 1 second-to-last in defensive success rate and DEAD LAST in opponent EPA per play, and the Giants converted NINE OF TEN THIRD DOWNS. Dallas also ranked 20th in run-stop win rate. Inside The Star's framing of the mood is 'urgency bordering on panic', noting 88% of teams that start 0-2 have missed the postseason since 2000 and that Dallas has not started 0-2 since 2010.
week1.src: NBC Sports Philadelphia Sep 13; SI Betting Sep 15; Inside The Star Sep 18 2026

injuries.read: The ledger modestly favours Washington. Dallas loses two defensive starters including its signal-caller and hands the green dot to a rookie — on a defence that just finished dead last in opponent EPA per play and allowed nine third-down conversions in ten. Washington has publicly said it intends to attack exactly that with disguised coverages and tempo. Washington loses Luvu and Okonkwo, which is real, but gets Armstrong back and has Payne, Oweh, Chaisson and Omenihu all trending to play. Neither quarterback is affected.

weather.text: Indoors — the roof is expected CLOSED, so weather should be a non-factor. Fantasy Alarm's Week 2 weather report on Sep 18 lists this among four closed-roof games where 'weather is a non-factor no matter how the sky looks outside'. No official team or league announcement on roof status was located, so treat that as a well-sourced media expectation rather than a confirmed decision. For reference if it did open: AccuWeather for Arlington on Sunday has a high of 98°F with a RealFeel of 101, south wind at 8 mph, and a 55% chance of a late-afternoon thunderstorm overlapping the 3:25 PM local window. The 98-degree heat and the storm risk both point strongly toward a closed roof, and the NFL rule permits closing when hazardous weather is anticipated.
weather.src: Fantasy Alarm NFL Week 2 weather report, Sep 18 2026; AccuWeather Arlington

venue.text: Dallas's home opener, and an NFC East game where the loser falls to 0-2 having lost both divisional games, two behind Philadelphia and the Giants. Dallas leads the all-time series 81-49-2, swept both 2025 meetings including a 30-23 Christmas Day win, and is 8-2 at home against Washington over the past decade and 15-5 overall. The week's flashpoint: the Cowboys' official social account posted an image of Jayden Daniels injured on the ground captioned 'some of our favorite moments vs. the Commanders', then deleted it — reaction was critical even among Dallas fans, and Washington's coaches may well use it.
venue.src: SI / OnSI Sep 17 and Sep 18; Yahoo Sports Sep 19 2026

voices.who: The starkest straight-up versus against-the-spread split of the weekend
voices.take: Straight up the analyst community is 28-3 Dallas (90%): MMQB 7-1, ESPN 9-2, CBS 7-0, NFL.com 5-0. Against the spread, essentially every source that took a position is on WASHINGTON — FOX's Geoff Schwartz on +4.5, OddsShopper on +4.5 ('the number I want against a favorite whose defense just let a rookie quarterback go 9 of 10 on third down'), the Covers AI model on +3.5, Dimers implicitly — and Athlon's four experts passed on the game entirely. Not one published ATS recommendation to lay the points with Dallas was found.

voices.who: Models straddle the market and lean Washington on the spread
voices.take: numberFire has Dallas at 68.6%, Dimers at 61.1% with a projected 26-23 — and Dimers has Dallas covering −3.5 only 45.1% of the time. nfelo's model line is Washington +4.0, identical to the market line, which means nfelo sees NO edge at the current number. ESPN FPI, Opta and PFF could not be retrieved. Every model expressing a spread opinion sides with Washington.

voices.who: The tactical read both sides agree on
voices.take: Washington's stated plan is to attack Dallas's rookie green-dot linebacker Jaishawn Barham with disguised coverages and tempo to force miscommunication, and to run outside rather than inside given Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark on the Dallas interior. Dan Quinn, who coordinated that defence from 2021 to 2023, on the Cowboys: '11 starters returning... that was evident in the game last week.' Dallas's own media mood is 'urgency bordering on panic' with an 0-2 start in view.

research.x_note: Reddit was unreachable — r/nfl, r/sportsbook, r/Commanders and r/cowboys all returned blocked — and Blogging The Boys is robots-disallowed, so genuine fan-forum sentiment is missing from this file. The closest proxy to live social sentiment is the Cowboys' deleted post about Jayden Daniels's injury, which Yahoo covered on Saturday morning and which drew criticism from Dallas fans as well as Washington ones.

tracks.intro: Two of Ahmed's rows are picked by Claude, each by a fixed method, and placed through the same form as everyone else. Neither is the System: the System needs a live Pinnacle line and sits out until the collector runs.

research.method: Bet whatever most people think will win — sportsbook ticket counts, prediction-market crowds, expert panels, Reddit and X — at the best Kalshi price for that side.
research.verdict: The most one-sided straight-up media consensus of the weekend at 28-3, backed by 65% of tickets and 84% of the money. Worth being precise about what the crowd actually believes here: it believes Dallas WINS. It does not believe Dallas covers — every published spread pick found was on Washington. This track buys the winner question, so it buys Dallas.

evidence.text: Stake: 2,000 contracts at 66¢ = $1,320, fee $31.42, $1,351.42 tied up. Break-even 67.57¢.

statistics.method: Estimate each outcome's probability from models and the sharpest sportsbook prices, subtract Kalshi's ask and fee, and bet the line with the best expected profit — if there is one.
statistics.pick: No bet — sat this one out
statistics.verdict: Skipped. Kalshi's Dallas at 65.35% sits within a quarter of a point of the best-of-market devigged 65.12% — the tightest agreement between Kalshi and the books on the entire board. The tempting angle is Washington against the spread, where every model that expressed an opinion sides with the Commanders. But nfelo's model line IS the market line at Washington +4.0, which is the cleanest statement available that there is no edge here, and Kalshi's +4.5 at 52¢ is already a hair rich against a devigged 50.8%-51.9%.

evidence.text: Moneyline: the best-of-market synthetic (Washington +180 at DraftKings with Dallas −200 at Hard Rock, 2.38% hold) gives Dallas 65.12%; the lowest-hold single book gives 64.29%. Kalshi normalizes to 65.35%. Buying Dallas at 66¢ is negative; buying Washington at 35¢ against a fair 34.9%-35.7% is between −0.1¢ and +0.7¢ against a 1.59¢ fee.

Spread: Kalshi's 'Dallas by over 4.5' at 49¢ against a book devig of 48.07%-49.25% is roughly fair to a cent rich. The Washington side costs 52¢ against a devigged 50.75%-51.93% — also a hair rich. Neither clears a 1.75¢ fee.

The strongest argument for Washington, and why it was not enough. Dimers has Dallas covering −3.5 only 45.1% of the time, which would make Washington +4.5 worth well over 55%. But Dimers also has Dallas at 61.1% to win, four points below the market — so its spread number is downstream of a moneyline view the rest of the market rejects. Taking the spread number while ignoring where it comes from would be cherry-picking.

The decisive number: nfelo's model line is Washington +4.0 against a market line of Washington +4.0. The most respected public NFL spread model available here is saying the market has it exactly right. That is a skip, not a bet.

Total: books devig to Over 49.78%-50.43% at 50.5; Kalshi asks 51¢ for the Over. About a cent rich before a 1.75¢ fee. The Over is also the heavily public side at 76-81% of money, which is not a reason to buy it.

Recorded honestly: the injury asymmetry — a rookie taking the green dot for a last-ranked defence, against an opponent publicly planning to attack exactly that — is a real argument that the market may be a half-point light on Washington. It is not a 1.75¢ argument, and this track does not bet stories.
